title: My First Job
description: A teenager describes her first summer job at a fruit shop.
instructions: Read the text about a first job, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: My name is Mai, and I am sixteen. Last summer, I got my first job at a fruit shop near my house. The owner, Mr Binh, needed help because his son was away. I worked there from Monday to Friday, from eight o'clock until one o'clock.

Every morning, I put the fresh fruit on the tables outside the shop. Then I helped customers and gave them their change. At first, I often made mistakes with the money. Mr Binh was patient and taught me to count it twice.

The work was hard on hot days, and my feet hurt in the evenings. But I liked talking to the customers. An old lady came every day to buy two bananas and tell me stories. Soon I knew the names of many people in my street.

At the end of the summer, I had enough money to buy a new bicycle. Mr Binh also gave me a big bag of mangoes as a present. I learned a lot about work and people. I hope I can work at the shop again next summer.

This year, Mr Binh's son came back home, but Mr Binh still wanted my help. 'The customers like you,' he said. So I worked at the shop again, but only on Saturdays during the school year. I also started to do new jobs. I wrote the prices on small boards, and I ordered fruit from the farm on the phone.

One Saturday, Mr Binh was ill, and he could not come to the shop. He called me early in the morning and asked me to open it alone. I was very nervous. But I remembered everything he taught me. I counted the money twice, and I did not make any mistakes. In the evening, Mr Binh called again and thanked me.

Now I want to study business at university. One day, I hope to have my own shop, maybe a cafe with fresh fruit juice. My parents say that the job at the fruit shop was better than any class at school. I think they are right. I learned to work hard, to be careful with money and to be kind to every customer.
